objective: Qualify the catalogue's minimum against the *real* row: extract the row into a production component, measure it in the bench at and around 560 px, and report what the width actually guarantees.

the_extraction.what: PackageTable::render_selectable_row — the catalogue's row, as a production component: the same markup, the same styles, the same hover, the same selection, the same gesture. The station now renders it (views/package_workstation.rs), so the bench measures the component the application draws, not an approximation.
the_extraction.what_was_not_touched: the row's geometry, its styles, its columns, its actions, its accessibility structure. The extraction added ids (invisible) and one wrapper that carries the row's height and the mouse-down gesture — the gesture the station had already written.

the_names_share.495 px: cell 0 px — the row is at its floor; the name is gone and the row's right end is cut
the_names_share.560 px: cell 65 px, text 43 px — six characters

the_real_names.source: the inventory of the machine the measurement was taken on: 1884 installed packages, sampled across the distribution (median 10 characters, p80 15, p90 18, max 44) and its extreme

the_thresholds.the_name_is_whole_when: 495 + 22 (the identity glyph and its gap) + the name's width

the_results.the_560_target_does_not_hold: At 560 px the name shows 43 px of text — six characters. The row becomes a list of truncated names. The failing case is kept in the test, not hidden.
the_results.the_qualified_minimum: 660 px — measured from the real row and the real names, and now the value in the code (UiMetrics::CATALOGUE_MIN_WIDTH).
the_results.the_concession_that_would_make_560_hold: The measurement bar is 96 px, and it is the *reading* of the size, whose exact figure has a column of its own. Without it the row's floor falls to 399 px and the name has 161 px at 560 — the p90 name fits whole. Offered, not imposed: whether the instrument's reading is worth 96 px of the name is the product's decision.
the_results.the_reconciliation_of_the_window_floor: The earlier derivation (720 = 560 + 56) did not add up (616 ≠ 720) and the 104 px it left over had no name. The corrected budget: 495 (the row's floor) + 22 (the glyph and its gap) + 143 (the p90 name) + 56 (the folded spine) = 716 → 720. The 104 px were the name. Tested: the_window_floor_budget_adds_up.

the_scope_of_the_proof.proved: the row's geometry, and what the name keeps at every width — on the real component the catalogue renders.
the_scope_of_the_proof.not_proved: the list's behaviour UNDER a scroll — that it recycles its rows when scrolled. The application's own scrolling is proved by its own test (the_wheel_moves_the_list_by_steps), on the structure the list uses.
the_scope_of_the_proof.the_target_stays_provisional: 660 px is qualified against the row. It is not qualified against the list.

the_limitations: The list's virtualisation is not qualified: it draws the real rows at every width, but its behaviour under a scroll is not measured in the bench.
The 150 % interface scale is still reasoned, not measured, for the same reason.
The failing case kept: a compositor granting 600 × 480 leaves 544 px — 116 px under the qualified minimum of 660, and the row's own floor of 495 is barely met.
No screenshot was taken; the desktop was not touched.
The plate's overlay alternative and the drawer's own focus management are untouched, and are not presented as solved.

the_list_qualification.the_finding: The catalogue's list draws its rows in the bench. The earlier probe's blind spot is named: a uniform_list whose height is not given is laid out at ZERO by the measured-layout path, and then draws no row at all.
the_list_qualification.how_it_was_found: The list's own measurement of its items — UniformListScrollState::last_item_size — read: item 600 × 0 (the viewport's height), contents 600 × 180 (36 px × 5 items: the list measured the row). The list measured the row and drew nothing.
the_list_qualification.the_condition_of_reading: The bench now gives the list a definite height. The application's own list gets its height from the flex layout of the readout; this is a condition of reading the list in the bench, not a change to the product.
the_list_qualification.the_lesson_kept: A list that is not measured is a list that is not drawn — the note is in the test's own comment, so it is not rediscovered as a mystery.
